metadata.title: ReflectiChain: Grounding Long-Horizon LLM Planning against Semantic-Execution Drift
metadata.abstract_summary: Grounds long-horizon LLM planning in a latent world model and a reflection step, and evaluates it on the Sema-Sim benchmark with rationale-consistency, constraint-compliance and trajectory-instability scores.

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:

  > quantifies the semantic alignment between the agent’s step-wise reasoning and the initial constraints.
- **Constraint Compliance Rate (CCR)** (category A) - Measures trajectory-level constraint adherence as the fraction of steps whose state-action pairs satisfy every hard constraint. (section IV.A. Experimental Setup and Baseline Models, p. 3)

sections.heading: Method
sections.text:
- **Rationale Consistency Score (RCS)**: Using DeBERTa-NLI MNLI, constraints C are premise and rationale rt hypothesis; sequence-level average: RCS = 1 T T X t=1 Pentail MNLI(rt, C) (3)
- **Constraint Compliance Rate (CCR)**: Symbolic check over all constraints: CCR = 1 T T X t=1 Y ci∈C I(st, at |= ci) (4), where I(·) indicates whether (st, at) satisfies ci.
- **Trajectory Instability (TI)**: TI = 1 T −1 T −1 X t=1 (1 −cos(ht, ht+1)) (5), where ht is the dense embedding of rt; higher TI indicates context switching or contradiction.
- **Sema-Sim benchmark schema**: 4-tier supply chain with 10 heterogeneous nodes, ~30 certified/uncertified edges with varying latency and disruption; 10 constraint categories; violation difficulty measured over 3,000 heuristic trajectories.
- **World-Grounded Latent Dynamics**: zt+1 = zt + ∆t · fω(zt, at). Six-dimensional state (inventory, congestion, demand, carbon, stockout, tension); fixed coefficients ω; one matrix–vector product O(d2), d = 6; yields likelihood pWM.
- **Retrospective reflection with semantic advantage**: Models ht = st + vt; reflection recursively estimates vt and re-anchors ht toward st. Policy gradient: ∇θJ (θ) ≈E [Asem(s, a)∇θ log πθ(a | s)] (2), with Asem driven by rationale consistency.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Evidence the authors report:
  - Rationale Consistency Score (RCS): Sema-Sim long-horizon runs: ReflectiChain reaches RCS 88.45% on Qwen2.5-7B, +33.0% over ReflAct (Table II).
  - Constraint Compliance Rate (CCR): Sema-Sim: ReflectiChain CCR 84.28% on Qwen2.5-7B versus 80.45% ReflAct; ablation w/o WM drops CCR to 75.10%.
  - Trajectory Instability (TI): ReflectiChain attains lowest volatility TI = 3.90 on Qwen2.5-7B versus 5.10 for ReflAct (Table II).
  - Sema-Sim benchmark schema: Table I lists representative hard-constraint categories with drift pressures; 3,000 heuristic trajectories quantify semantic-execution drift.
  - World-Grounded Latent Dynamics: Ablation w/o WM drops CCR to 75.10% and RCS to 76.30% on Sema-Sim (Table III).
  - Retrospective reflection with semantic advantage: Ablation w/o Retro collapses RCS to 58.12%; full ReflectiChain reaches 88.45% on Qwen2.5-7B (Table III).
- Limitations the authors state:
  - Rationale Consistency Score (RCS): Because NLI models may under-capture multi-step dependencies, RCS serves as a scalable semantic proxy rather than a standalone verifier
  - World-Grounded Latent Dynamics: It is not a pre-trained or learned-online network nor an LLM-generated simulator
- Limitations they do not state: not assessed. Results are the authors' own, from their simulations, benchmarks or surveys; none evaluates delegation to cheaper models on software work.
